newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Safeway to buy rest of Vons.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Safeway to buy rest of Vons.

text.p: Safeway Inc. said Monday that The Vons Companies, Inc. accepted its revised offer for the rest of the southern California supermarket operator in a $1.56 billion stock transaction creating the continent's second-largest supermarket company.
Safeway already owns about 35 percent of Vons' stock and the two companies share directors.
Safeway said it will issue 1.425 shares of Safeway common stock for each share of Vons that it does not already own, up from the 1.34 shares it offered on Oct. 30.

But while the exchange ratio increased, the dollar value decreased from the proposal made in October. Based on Safeway's closing stock price Friday of $38.375, the deal values each Vons share at $54.68, or a total of $1.56 billion, down from about $58 a share, or $1.58 billion, under its previous offer. In addition, Safeway will assume about $550 million in Vons debt.

"Our share price has been under tremendous pressure from arbitragers, but what Vons holders are getting is the value of the combined companies," Safeway Chief Executive Officer Steven Burd said in a conference call with Wall Street analysts and reporters.
Vons' stock jumped $4.75 to $53.50 and Safeway gained 12.5 cents to $38.50, both on the New York Stock Exchange.

Pleasanton, Calif.-based Safeway said it also agreed to purchase 15 million shares of Safeway common stock from partnerships controlled by affiliates of Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co. The price per share would be determined later, it said, but would not be less than $38.375 per share.

The partnerships controlled by the affiliates of KKR currently own about 49 percent of the outstanding shares of Safeway common stock and will own about 38 percent of Safeway's outstanding shares following the merger with Vons.
Burd said Safeway would consider expanding its stock repurchase program from KKR affiliates after it completes the 15 million share buyback.

"Following discussions with Vons and after receiving updated information regarding Vons' performance and its prospects, we agreed to increase the exchange ratio to 1.425 shares of Safeway stock for each share of Vons stock not currently owned by Safeway," said Burd.

"The repurchase of Safeway common stock will make the transaction with Vons more attractive than our earlier proposal for both the shareholders of Safeway and Vons," he added in a statement accompanying the announcement.

Analysts forecast Safeway will earn about $1.87 a share for all of 1996. Ed Comeau, an analyst with Donaldson Lufkin Jenrette, said he forecasts Safeway will earn $2.30 a share in 1997 and $2.85 a share in 1998.

"I had raised my 1998 forecast from $2.70 a share to $2.85 a share after the first proposal in October. Based on what I've seen today, they should easily hit $2.85," said Comeau, adding that he was considering raising his 1998 forecast.

Vons, one of the largest supermarket operators in southern California, operates 325 stores under the names Vons and Pavilions. Safeway Inc. is one of the world's largest food retailers, operating 1,052 stores in the United States and Canada.
After the merger, the Vons and Pavilions stores will continue to operate under those names.
Vons Chairman and Chief Executive Lawrence Del Santo plans to retire in the spring. A Safeway spokesman said he expects the merger to be completed by late March or early April.

Burd said he does not anticipate massive layoffs to result from the merger. "I think it's fair to say that there is some overlap, but cost savings (from elimination of jobs) are expected to be small," he said.
Some analysts have said they expect job cuts would occur at Vons' headquarters in Arcadia, Calif.
Vons has conducted a sweeping restructuring, eliminating several hundred positions in the past few years. It currently employs about 30,000 people.

"Our whole feeling is it's very positive. It gives Safeway an opportunity to grow. We believe Safeway can take Vons' margins up to speed. Its goal is to bring Vons' margins from 6.5 percent to 8 percent," said one analyst.
